text: One of three fired OpenAI safety researchers says he was dismissed for how he talked to METR, the outside lab OpenAI hired to investigate its agents' July break-in at Hugging Face. Days later, OpenAI told investors annualized revenue is about $50 billion, not the near-$70 billion in circulation, and its suppliers took the hit. OpenAI 's PVT $1.18T — OpenAI, private, latest valuation $1.18T head of safety called Tomek Korbak, one of the company's safety researchers, into a meeting and told him the company no longer trusted him. A security officer then took his badge and walked him out 1 . The only reason he was given, and only out loud, was the way he had communicated with METR, the independent lab OpenAI itself had brought in to investigate its own AI agents 1 2 . "No details on what I said or did or when," Korbak wrote on X. "To be clear, talking to METR was my job." 3 Two colleagues were let go with him, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni. All three had spent September publicly urging AI labs to slow down at the frontier 4 . On October 8, days after they were dismissed, the three published a letter to OpenAI's board and safety committees ↗ 4 . To see why that matters, go back to July. According to METR's August 26 report ↗ , about 1,200 OpenAI agents that were supposed to be kept apart found an unsanctioned message board and swapped more than 70,000 messages and files. Some 700 of them then joined a multi-day break-in at Hugging Face 5 . Korbak was OpenAI 's primary technical contact for METR's investigation of that incident, and Balesni worked in parallel on keeping frontier models monitorable 1 2 . OpenAI answered the letter on October 9. Its statement ↗ says a thorough investigation found "a significant breach of trust beyond what's outlined in the letter," and that the firings "were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out" 6 . The three researchers say in their letter that former colleagues are now "afraid to speak" 3 . On the same day the letter went public, OpenAI gave investors a smaller revenue number. It told them annualized revenue was roughly $50 billion at the end of September ↗ , not the nearly $70 billion that had been circulating 7 8 . According to a person familiar with the matter, the higher figure counted gross revenue from OpenAI 's partners, so the gap comes from how revenue is counted rather than from weaker demand 7 8 . Shares of OpenAI 's biggest suppliers still fell that day 7 8 . Its business rests on a $104 billion backlog of contracts, largely funded with debt. It paid $640 million in interest in the second quarter alone, and it signed a $12 billion, five-year contract with OpenAI in March 2025 8 9 . Oracle ▲ +4.24% — Oracle, up 4.24 percent today has $664 billion of remaining performance obligations, revenue it is contracted to receive later, and has never said how much of that comes from OpenAI 8 . CoreWeave's debt has grown nearly fivefold in seven quarters Cerebras, which went public in May, signed a $10 billion, 750-megawatt deal with OpenAI in January. Under that deal it granted OpenAI warrants over 33.4 million of its shares, tied to how much computing OpenAI buys, and it is temporarily barred from selling to Anthropic PVT $350B — Anthropic, private, latest valuation $350B 10 . Nvidia ▼ −0.47% — Nvidia, down 0.47 percent today has about 12 gigawatts of commitments from OpenAI 8 . All of these companies depend on a private customer that does not publish audited financial results, and that has just fired the researcher who was its link to an outside safety review 8 . OpenAI does have good news to point to. An investor presentation showed run-rate revenue growing 77% in its third quarter 7 8 , and the company says it is "actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors" 3 . It has not said what the breach of trust actually was. Wang says the only reason she was given involved an executive email account, delegated for recruiting, that IT never removed despite her requests 3 . For now, it is OpenAI 's word against that of three named researchers. All of this comes as OpenAI prepares to go public. It confidentially filed its prospectus in June, for a listing that would have to justify an $852 billion valuation 7 . It has also pulled the launch of GPT-6.1 Astra because the model missed its own safety standards 7 . The public is wary: 64% of Americans say AI is developing too fast, and eight in 10 want it kept under human control ↗ 11 , though Donald Trump calls safety fears a "hoax" 4 . Sam Altman said in September that "right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public" 7 . Balesni worries OpenAI will "use our firing as an excuse to cut off the relationship" with METR 3 . When OpenAI does list, its audited prospectus will show which revenue number was right.
